question.:question/problem:
Calculate $CA-CB$, where
$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & -1 & -3\end{bmatrix}$
$B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & -1 & -3\end{bmatrix}$
$C=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -3 & -1\end{bmatrix}$
Fill in the missing entries.
$CA-CB=$
$0${{field-2}}$0$
{{field-1}}{{field-3}}$0$
$0$$0$$0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Keep the common factor $C$ on the left and preserve the order of the subtraction:

$$
CA-CB=C(A-B).
$$

Combine corresponding entries first:

$$
A-B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The combined matrix is zero, so the entire product is zero.

$$
CA-CB=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Keep the common factor $C$ on the right and preserve the order of the subtraction:

$$
BC-AC=(B-A)C.
$$

Combine corresponding entries first:

$$
B-A=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use row-by-column multiplication on the shorter product $(B-A)C$.

$$
\begin{aligned}(BC-AC)_{32}&=(1)(1)+(-1)(-2)=3 \\ (BC-AC)_{31}&=(1)(-1)+(-1)(3)=-4 \\ (BC-AC)_{11}&=(-1)(1)+(1)(-1)=-2 \\ (BC-AC)_{12}&=(-1)(-2)+(1)(1)=3\end{aligned}
$$



$$
BC-AC=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -4 & -4 \\ -4 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
